summary: Mangal Deva Shastri was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell at the University of Oxford, earning his D.Phil. in 1922. He later served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from circa 1937 to 1946.

Working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology, Manik Man Bajracharya studied at Tribhuvan University, Metropolia UAS, and HTW Berlin. He held posts at HTW Berlin, Metropolia, the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and Heidelberg University.
Manilal Patel was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Marburg, where he studied under Johannes Nobel.

Manish Sinha, a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, earned his Ph.D. at Magadh University in 1999. He became a professor there in 1996, serving as department head (2018–2021), and was an INTACH convener in 2021.

Manit Akkhachat is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a B.A. from Ramkhamhaeng University and a Ph.D. from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University in 2022. He served as a lecturer at Nakhon Ratchasima Rajabhat University beginning in 2013.

Manjiri Bhalerao works in history, archaeology, and Indology, having studied at Deccan College and Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth. She became an associate professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth in 2004 and is attested as visiting faculty at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Manlio Iofrida is a philosopher who studied at the University of Pisa and the Scuola Normale Superiore from circa 1970 to 1975. He held academic positions at the University of Pisa (circa 1981–1987) and the University of Bologna (circa 1988).

Manshi Kiyozawa was a Japanese philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa. He served as the first dean and founding president of Otani University from 1901 to 1902.

Manu Leumann was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD under Albert Thumb at Strasbourg and studied with Wackernagel, Andreas, and Schulze. He worked at the Thesaurus Linguae Latinae and served as professor at the University of Zurich (1927–1959).

id: P:Manuel Antonio Ato del Avellanal Carrera
summary: Manuel Antonio Ato del Avellanal Carrera studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara and SOAS University of London. He has lectured in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and theology of religions at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru and Universidad del Pacífico.

Manuel Sassmann is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Stuttgart and Heidelberg University. He has served as a research fellow at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

id: P:Manuel de la Revilla y Moreno
summary: Manuel de la Revilla y Moreno was a Spanish scholar of philosophy who studied under Francisco García Ayuso at the Complutense University of Madrid. He held academic posts at the Universidad Central and became Professor of Literary History at Complutense in 1876.

Marbury Bladen Ogle studied classics and linguistics at Johns Hopkins University under Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve and Maurice Bloomfield. He held professorships and department chairs in Latin and Classical languages at the universities of Vermont, Ohio State, and Minnesota.

Marc Aurel Stein, who worked in archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, studied at Vienna, Leipzig, Tübingen, and Oxford under Rudolf von Roth. His posts included Principal of Oriental College and Archaeological Surveyor for the Archaeological Survey of India.
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Lausanne in 2016, studying under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst and teacher Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Matthew T. Kapstein, Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Cohen was a French linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. Over his career, he held teaching posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris from the 1910s to 1954.

Marcel Granet was a French sinologist who studied under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. He founded the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises and held professorships at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes.

Marcel Hofinger was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate under Étienne Lamotte at KU Leuven. He served as a professor of Greek language and literature at KU Leuven and taught at Université catholique de Louvain (1946–1983).

Marcel Mauss was a French scholar of religion and sociology who studied under Émile Durkheim, Sylvain Lévi, and Antoine Meillet. He held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1901–1940) and the Collège de France (1931–1941).
